target_customer: Satellite operators, space agencies (NASA) and defense customers such as the US Space Force
problem: Moving satellites and handling debris or asteroid resources in orbit is expensive with chemical or electric propulsion, and faint fast-moving objects are hard to detect.
business_model: Government R&D contracts and SBIR awards now, with planned orbital logistics services and space domain awareness data sales
product_category: Space propulsion, orbital transfer vehicles and telescopes

founders.name: Joel Sercel
prior_employers: NASA JPL (per search summary, not opened)
education: PhD space propulsion and plasma physics, Caltech
founders.background_notes: Education from the YC page. Momentus CTO tenure through 2019 from SpaceNews coverage of August 2021. Company founding year differs by source (YC page 2016, other sources 2015).

competitors.name: Momentus
competitors.what: Space tug and in-space transportation (Vigoride) company founded earlier and a YC alumnus; SpaceNews framed TransAstra as a competing space logistics venture

technical_complexity.rationale: Solar thermal propulsion that vaporizes water or other fluids, a new orbital transfer vehicle and a novel telescope with custom tracking software; hardware and flight qualification are research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: The company cites five issued patents and more than a dozen pending on its YC page, and the hardware is hard to replicate; it has not yet proven flight performance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows anyone copying or acquiring it; it continued to win SBIR and NASA awards through 2025.

market_need_then: In 2021 the in-space economy was growing with rideshare launches and a push for orbital debris and space domain awareness; the company cited Space Force interest in detecting dark fast-moving objects between Earth and the Moon.

branding.domain_note: Uses transastra.com; SpaceNews in 2021 referred to the firm as TransAstronautica, so naming varied.

identity.mascot_or_character: Bee theme across vehicles: Worker Bee, Mini Bee, Honey Bee, Queen Bee
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, ambitious, patent and cost-claim heavy

branding.brand_signature: Bee-themed spacecraft family and the Omnivore propulsion name

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable product names, but press mentions the company mostly through Sercel's Momentus history, and no community or merch evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: TransAstra is an active, long-horizon space hardware company led by a propulsion PhD and former Momentus CTO. After YC in Summer 2021 and a reported 4M seed it has relied on SBIR, Space Force and NASA awards, including a 5M combined NASA and private round in September 2025, rather than large venture rounds. Its path depends on flight demonstrations that are still in development.
notes: transastra.com fetch returned only the title (likely script-rendered), so the company site was not readable. The 4M seed figure comes from search summaries of SpaceNews and related coverage, plus an aggregator; I could not open the SpaceNews text, so treat it as lightly verified. Aggregators disagree on totals (7.0M, 14.4M, 15.6M, CB Insights 3.37M); none recorded. The 2025 round mixes a NASA contract award with private investment, so it is labeled other. SBIR awards (2022 NASA and DoD, 2023 Space Force Phase One) are grants not recorded as rounds because amounts were not opened. Sercel's JPL employment is from a search summary only and is not listed as sourced; the YC page does not name employers.
